maps.title: Chicago, drawn by J. S. Wright according to survey, 1834
maps.creator: John Stephen Wright
maps.publisher: Historic Urban Plans, Ithaca, New York (facsimile)
maps.coverage: Original Town, Wabansia, Kinzie's Addition, the School Section and the harbour
maps.credit_line: Facsimile of J. S. Wright's 1834 manuscript survey. The original drawing is public domain and held by the National Archives, Washington, D.C.; the sheet shown here is the Historic Urban Plans, Ithaca, reproduction of it. The open-rights sibling scan of the same drawing is the Boston Public Library / Leventhal copy, commonwealth:js9577436, which source_url links to.
maps.notes: The survey Hathaway's 1834 sheet derives from, and the master geometry source of the 4D reconstruction. The printed caption records the sheet's wear: "Signs of wear are apparent. Two portions are missing, the larger being near the lower center. At one time the drawing was torn to this spot from the upper right margin. Later the manuscript was mounted on cloth to repair this tear" - nothing inside those two losses is Wright's ink. Georeferenced in this project: the BPL master's control is chicago/4d/data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_gcps.json, and this 5050x6628 px sheet is registered in its own pixel space in chicago/4d/data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_nara_hup_gcps.json (source id wright_1834_nara_hup). The two scans are one drawing photographed twice, and neither is a second witness to the other.

media.title: Chicago In Early Days, 1779-1857 (fifteen-panel retrospective sheet)
media.credit_line: Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, Chicago; chromolithograph, copyright 1893
media.notes: Fifteen numbered vignettes with a printed key: 1 Old Fort Dearborn erected 1803; 2 the first cabin built 1779 by Jean Baptiste Point de Saible; 3 Chicago in 1845; 4 First Rush Medical College; 5 Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835, population 3,265; 6 the first court house; 7 Water Works erected 1853; 8 Chicago in 1830 from the lake, population 96; 9 Wolf Point in 1830; 10 the Clybourne House; 11 the Green Tree Hotel, corner West Lake and Canal, built 1833; 12 the old Kinzie Mansion, built 1832; 13 Chicago in 1853; 14 the Sauganash Hotel, built 1831; 15 the old block house and light house in 1857, the last of Fort Dearborn. Panel 14 shows the Sauganash as a two-story frame block with an attached single-story log wing and NO full-width gallery - evidence in the long-running dispute over whether the hotel had a porch.
media.creator: Kurz & Allison
media.repository: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
media.accuracy_note: Made in 1893, sixty to a hundred years after the scenes depicted, and not from eyewitness records. Its panel dates are also unreliable - it dates the Kinzie Mansion to 1832, which contradicts every documentary source. Useful as an inventory of what nineteenth-century Chicago believed its early buildings looked like; not a measured architectural record.

media.title: Chicago from the lake, looking west, with Fort Dearborn and the sandbar
media.credit_line: Hand-coloured lithograph, later nineteenth century; exact publication not identified
media.notes: The standard retrospective view of the settlement from the lake: the palisaded Fort Dearborn compound on the south bank with its flagstaff, the Kinzie house group on the north bank, and - the reason this image matters for landscape work - the long sandbar deflecting the river mouth southward, with the low prairie and scattered riverside timber behind.
media.creator: Unidentified
media.repository: Unverified - re-source from the holding institution before republication
media.accuracy_note: A retrospective view, not drawn from life at the depicted date. Its value here is topographic rather than architectural: the sandbar, shoreline and river geometry it records agree with the documentary accounts. Publication details are not established - treat attribution as unconfirmed.

media.title: Map of Chicago in 1812
media.credit_line: Engraved plate, A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 1 (1884)
media.notes: Labels the pre-settlement landscape: Prairie, S. Branch, N. Branch, Indian Trail, Agency House, Burns, Ouilmette, Kinzies, Fort D., Sand Hills and Lake Michigan. Shows the timber distribution as tree symbols - heavy on the north and north-east, following the river west - and the sand hills along the lakeshore south of the fort. Corroborates the documentary description of the timber belt and the dune ridge.
media.creator: A. T. Andreas
media.accuracy_note: Drawn in 1884 to illustrate 1812 - a reconstruction, and it predates the target period of most of this dataset by two decades. Reliable for coarse landscape structure and for house and trail positions; not a survey.

media.title: An imaginary view of the site of Chicago in 1779, showing the cabin of Jean Baptiste Point de Saible
media.credit_line: Plate engraved by Moss Eng. Co., New York; copyright A. T. Andreas, 1884
media.notes: Panoramic view of the river mouth with insets of the du Sable cabin and a portrait captioned as the first settler. Shows the deflected river mouth, the bar, open prairie with scattered oaks, and a Native encampment at left.
media.creator: A. T. Andreas
media.accuracy_note: The plate calls itself 'an imaginary view' in its own caption - the most honest label in this collection, and it should be taken literally. The portrait inset is likewise not an authenticated likeness of du Sable. Use for landscape character only.
